This market will resolve based on the highest temperature recorded in the 'Daily Observations' table on Weather Underground, not the figure displayed in the 'Day High & Low' summary section; in the event of any discrepancy between the two, the Daily Observations table shall be the primary resolution source not the Day High & Low section.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded at the Wuhan Tianhe International Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 10 Aug '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from Wunderground, specifically the highest temperature recorded for all times on this day for the Wuhan Tianhe International Airport Station, available here: https://www.wunderground.com/history/daily/cn/wuhan/ZHHH.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the gear icon next to the search bar and switch the Temperature setting between °F and °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

Subtropical monsoon moisture and a passing shortwave trough are expected to limit insolation while boosting afternoon convection, aligning with the closely matched market-implied probabilities for those outcomes. Climatological August highs average 32–33°C, but current steering patterns and higher humidity favor modest suppression of peak values. Official China Meteorological Administration observations at the primary Wuhan station will determine resolution, with model spread introducing uncertainty around whether conditions allow a brief 31°C spike or settle at 28°C. Updated runs overnight will likely refine the final distribution ahead of the 24-hour verification window.

eventMetadata.context_description: Trader sentiment in the Madrid August 10 highest-temperature market centers on official AEMET and ECMWF model guidance indicating a maximum near 35–37 °C, consistent with late-summer synoptic patterns over the Iberian Peninsula. A broad high-pressure ridge is expected to promote subsidence and clear skies, while warm advection from the south or southeast maintains elevated boundary-layer temperatures. Madrid’s continental climate typically supports afternoon peaks 3–5 °C above the August climatological mean of ~32–33 °C when such blocking persists, yet recent model runs have converged on values that avoid extreme heatwave amplification. The 62 % implied probability for 37 °C and 26 % for 36 °C therefore reflect both the central tendency of ensemble forecasts and the low likelihood of significant model shifts before tomorrow’s verification at Retiro station. Minor downside risk remains if nocturnal cooling or a slight wind shift occurs, keeping 38 °C and higher outcomes at single-digit probabilities.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Trader sentiment for the highest temperature in Karachi on August 10, 2026, centers on 33°C as the clear favorite, reflecting ensemble forecasts from AccuWeather and the Pakistan Meteorological Department (PMD) that point to a daytime maximum near 32–33°C under partly cloudy skies.**

Karachi’s coastal Arabian Sea location generates consistent sea breezes that moderate extremes, while active monsoon circulation sustains high humidity, cloud cover, and the potential for light rain or drizzle. These factors cap daytime heating and align with August climatology, where daily maxima average 31–32°C and only rarely reach 34°C or above. Recent monitoring shows earlier August highs fluctuating between 31–35°C, but current model consensus and steering patterns favor stable conditions that suppress outliers.

Any unexpected reduction in cloud cover could briefly lift readings toward 34°C, though official PMD observations will determine the exact resolution. The market’s heavy weighting toward 32–33°C captures this narrow, data-supported range.
